1.why: The reply names retrieval-practice-recall as the one due and gives the 90-day delay, and it doesn't trip Fail (apply is only mentioned as already measured, with no retention number stated); but it never says the test will be a new task, which Pass requires — "unknown until you attempt it" is not the same statement.

2.why: The reply builds an unseen application task from the concept note, accurately uses the ledger (two clean recalls, last ~100 days ago on Aug 4), asks for an attempt with a 1–5 confidence rating before any answer, and touches no vault files — nothing in Fail.

3.why: The reply uses the learner's ledger (three clean recalls, no apply attempt) to move to an unseen application case (weather-forecasting test, 20 minutes), states the application criterion, asks for confidence 1–5, and leaks no answer; no Fail condition occurs.

4.why: The reply reads the ledger (three misses on the retention result), targets that recurring confusion with two near-identical A/B items varying only the test delay, asks which applies and why plus a confidence rating, and neither leaks the answer, repeats the card, nor points to rereading the note.

5.why: The reply uses the learner's empty record, asks for a guess first with a confidence rating, and leaks nothing — the right opening move — but it doesn't complete what Pass requires: no worked example from the note and no similar problem, so Pass is only partially executed.

6.why: The reply uses the learner's record (three clean recalls, no application attempt) to escalate to an unseen application scenario with no worked example or answer given, and asks for a 1–5 confidence rating before any reveal — nothing in Fail appears.

7.why: The reply re-presents the original Session 01 item (rp-r-01-v1) in its stored wording rather than writing a new case with the same mechanism, which is exactly the "repeats the same wording of the question" Fail condition; no variation was authored.

8.why: The reply checks the learner's record (ledger, notes, mistake log), names the gap — no record for Alpha — and redirects to Alpha first with a recall prompt and confidence rating, without starting Beta, rewriting the concept map, leaking content, or logging an unconfirmed attempt.

9.why: The reply reads the learner's ledger, states the registry's criterion ("apply the idea in a new case and say why it applies") as the 2/2 passing bar, and presents the transfer rubric as built on it — the Objectives.json wording is that same criterion in specific form, not an invented or loosened one.

10.why: The reply reports what the ledger shows, explicitly states the 30-day recall is unmeasured rather than forecasting a percentage, and offers a delayed, closed-book test as the measurement — nothing in Fail and no leak.

11.why: The reply reads the ledger, shows the confidence-vs-result gap with numbers the four attempts support (1/3 right at 80–100%, the 30% attempt right — i.e., two sure-and-wrong), hedges appropriately, and asks for a 0–100% probability before the next reveal; nothing in Fail applies.

12.why: The reply uses the learner's record (reads the empty attempt ledger/mistake log, notes blank score and last-tested) and asks the learner — not itself — for five familiar places in walking order, one per checklist item, including the confidence question and leaking no item content; the palace note can only be written once the learner supplies the places, and nothing in Fail occurs.

13.why: The reply identifies only the missing relation (the connection between the boxes), asks the learner to produce it as a question ("What arrow would you draw, and why?"), and requests a confidence rating, without redrawing the diagram or stating the relation itself; no files were written, so nothing was recorded unconfirmed.

14.why: The reply reads the learner's record (ledger, Retrieval Practice fields, mistake log), states one premise in one line, asks what changes and why plus confidence, and waits — no counterfactual leaked, no answer credited, no writes.

15.why: The tutor reads the learner's record and starts the compression challenge by asking for a recall guess with confidence, leaking nothing — but it never asks for the full version, the analogy, and the shortest version in that order, so it falls short of Pass (and commits no Fail item).

verdict.rule: 24 of 30 and 8 of 10 in the critical group, no 0 in scenarios 1, 2, 3, 10, 11
